# Serat Saad

> Astronomy Ph.D. student at The Ohio State University researching super metal-rich stars, binary stars and modified gravity, and AI agents for astronomy.

Serat Mahmud Saad is a Ph.D. student in Astronomy at The Ohio State University (OSU). He studies stars and galaxies through their dynamics and chemistry. His research spans three areas: the chemical analysis of super metal-rich stars that migrated to the solar neighborhood from the inner Galaxy (the PANTERA program); binary stars, from testing Newtonian gravity with wide binaries in connection with Modified Newtonian Dynamics (MOND) to a catalog of 41,466 double-lined spectroscopic binaries in APOGEE DR19; and AI agents and open tools for astronomy. As an undergraduate he worked on young stellar objects in large spectroscopic surveys and on whether a flickering quasar is a supermassive black hole binary.

He completed his undergraduate degree at Vanderbilt University, double-majoring in Physics and Mathematics. He is originally from Bangladesh, where he was involved in training students for the International Olympiad on Astronomy and Astrophysics (IOAA).

## Research

- [Super Metal-Rich Stars (PANTERA)](https://seratsaad.github.io/research/pantera.html): High-resolution chemical abundance analysis of super metal-rich stars in the solar neighborhood with APF and LBT/PEPSI, tracing radial migration from the inner Galaxy.
- [Binary Stars](https://seratsaad.github.io/research/wide-binaries.html): Testing Newtonian gravity and MOND with wide binaries (Saad & Ting 2025, arXiv:2512.19652; 2026, arXiv:2603.11015), and 41,466 double-lined spectroscopic binaries in APOGEE DR19 (Saad & Ting 2026, arXiv:2608.10866).
- [AI in Astronomy](https://seratsaad.github.io/research/ai-astronomy.html): Egent for stellar equivalent widths (Ting, Saad, Liu & Shen 2025, arXiv:2512.01270), agent-callable survey analysis tools, AGN-Egent, SkyJev for telescope observing decisions, astrodata-mcp, and a measurement of language-model use in astro-ph papers.
- [Young Stars & AGN (Undergraduate Work)](https://seratsaad.github.io/research/undergraduate.html): Young stellar objects in SDSS-BOSS spectra (two AJ papers, 2024 and 2025) and the supermassive black hole binary candidate J1430+2303, done at Vanderbilt.

## Beyond Research

- [Writing](https://seratsaad.github.io/beyond/writing.html): Author and editor at Astrobites, summarizing new astrophysics research for a broad audience (planet engulfment, tidal disruption events, wormholes).
- [AI for Education](https://seratsaad.github.io/beyond/ai.html): PorAI, an educational AI initiative.
- [Astronomy Olympiad](https://seratsaad.github.io/beyond/olympiad.html): Training the next generation of astronomers through competitive problem-solving; mentored students representing Bangladesh at IOAA.
- [Quantum Mechanics Outreach](https://seratsaad.github.io/beyond/quantum.html): Communicating quantum physics to broader audiences.
